signals: current-sensor (BJB) phase-current ripple waveform at high motor speed; motor speed; PEB torque-cut / fail-safe state
note: Current sensor in junction box misdiagnoses a gap in motor current-ripple frequency at high speed; inverter cuts torque. Remedy: inverter fail-safe software. Description of cause NR. Seeing the ripple gap needs a high-rate current trace before the trip; a snapshot shows only the fault state. RMISC attachment image-only (no text).

signals: none (locates only: front-end noise, suspension failure)
note: Under-torqued steer-axle spring-hanger fasteners found by plant quality control.

signals: none (locates only: pretensioner non-deployment in a crash)
note: Pretensioner clutch pawls and O-ring missing from assembly; found at supplier deployment test and teardown.

signals: LDC (12 V converter) output voltage at charge-cycle start and end; MOSFET / power-stage temperature; coolant and fan state over the charge or drive; ICCU fuse state
note: ICCU low-voltage converter MOSFET fails: two stated causes, overvoltage at start and end of the battery charging cycle (transient) and thermal loading during charging and driving (minutes). Window set by the thermal-loading leg; the rate by the overvoltage transient. Evidence: returned-part inspection and CT scan.

signals: inverter phase/DC current versus broadcast current limit; battery current; contactor state; SOC (regen at high SOC)
note: Inverter firmware mis-estimates broadcast current, overshoots the current limit, battery contactors open. Over-current is an electrical event, so not software-only.

signals: none (locates only: string-open / fuse-blown warning, abnormal module voltage and temperature)
note: Inadequate weld penetration on a busbar (J-bar) inside the battery module separates, arcs and overheats a cell; co-cause: BMS software does not lock out the pack. The remedy detects high-resistance behaviour from voltage and temperature, so a signal could flag a bad joint but not the stated cause (weld penetration). Defective part is inside the traction-battery module, hence out-of-scope flag; BMS software co-cause is in scope.

signals: none (locates only: wheel-nut crack / wheel looseness)
note: Center-lock wheel nut cracks: lack of fusion in Tier-2 hollow aluminium extrusion.

signals: ICCU / LDC output and HV-side voltage transients; power-stage temperature history across charge and drive cycles; 12 V battery voltage
note: ICCU damaged over time by transient high voltage and thermal cycling (two stated causes; document states cumulative damage over time, hence >700 s). Chronology is field-case counts only.

signals: HEV ECU output-limit value versus BMS output-limit demand; HV battery and cell voltage; accelerator pedal position; EV-mode flag; battery temperature
note: HEV ECU output-limit calculation does not follow the battery output-limit demand; rapid pedal after cold EV-mode driving pulls cell voltage below threshold, system ready-off. Freeze frame showed EV mode and cold; mechanism found on chassis dynamometer. Seeing limit vs demand over the pedal tip-in needs seconds. Defective module is the vehicle-level hybrid control ECU, so out-of-scope flagged (judgement).

signals: none (locates only: airbag deployment anomaly in a crash)
note: Passenger airbag score-line possibly missing on three instrument panels; supplier production-tracking error. Identified from production data.

signals: none (locates only: buckle rattle / restraint performance in a crash)
note: Seat-belt buckle bolt not torqued; supplier torque-controller attributed another bolt reading.

signals: isolation-fault DTC and fault-severity class at the trip; HV shutdown state; gear state
note: Vehicle control software misclassifies a loss of isolation as a severe fault and shuts the HV system in motion. The DTC set and the shutdown state at the trip identify it. Isolation loss is an electrical event, so not software-only. Defective module is the vehicle/powertrain controller, so out-of-scope flagged (judgement).

signals: none (locates only: misalignment / steering pull)
note: Wheel-alignment ring installed at the wrong angle at the plant; found by inspection. Description of cause NR but the defect text states the assembly error.

signals: none (locates only: HV shutdown / short at disconnect-switch terminals)
note: Fuse-box / disconnect-switch bracket fatigues under switch mass and vibration and breaks; terminals short to chassis. Mechanical design weakness; the defective part is a bracket.

signals: LDC/ICCU current and output voltage (over-current, end-of-charge overvoltage peak); power-stage and coolant temperature, water-pump state over charge or drive; ICCU fuse state
note: ICCU (24V-204 and ODI PE23011 closing resume): three stated causes, over-current, overvoltage at end of HV charging, thermal loading during operation. Window set by the thermal-loading leg; rate by the transients. Evidence: heat-damaged FETs on warranty returns; replication attempted.

signals: crash-sensor pulse and ACU deployment decision recorded at the event (EDR)
note: Airbag control unit calibration deploys seat-mounted side airbags in frontal crashes with little lateral offset. The crash pulse and deployment record at the event identify it.

signals: cell-module voltage and self-discharge trend across parked periods and charge cycles; module temperature
note: HV cell modules may self-discharge (supplier deviations; shifted electrodes in recalled sub-populations) and go into thermal propagation; root cause stated as not clear. Vehicle data showed the self-discharge-detection software would have warned months ahead, so the stated mechanism (self-discharge) is observable as a long trend. Defective part is the cell module (out of scope); BMS software is the co-component.

signals: none (locates only: panel detachment at airbag deployment)
note: Insufficient vibration-weld adhesion of instrument-panel topper to airbag chute doors (supplier heat, power fluctuation, mat misalignment); part recreated by DOE.

signals: none (locates only: handling / ride-height anomaly)
note: Supplier mislabelled rear suspension modules; wrong module installed.

signals: none (locates only: disconnect fails to fire at a crash or battery event)
note: Non-functioning pyrotechnic battery disconnect shipped through a traceability gap on a new supplier line; found in a validation test. HV disconnect counted in scope (contactor / junction function).

signals: pack / contactor current during wide-open-pedal and DC fast-charge events; contactor temperature and resistance history across sessions
note: BEC main-contactor design and part variation not robust to heat from multiple wide-open-pedal and DC fast-charge events; accumulated heat damage and wear lead to arcing, failure to close or weld. The document states accumulation over multiple events, hence >700 s. Remedy is junction-box replacement; ODI RQ23004 resumes read.

signals: none (locates only: axle shift / clunk)
note: Torque tool falsely signalled final torque on transverse torque-rod fasteners; assembly error.

signals: 12 V rail voltage transients during the HLCM software upgrade; HLCM phase current and status (DTC)
note: 12 V voltage fluctuations during a software upgrade damage one of two HLCM (DC-DC) phases; converter capacity halves; later loss of propulsion. Taking the event as the phase damage, the 12 V transient seconds before identifies it. If the event were the later propulsion loss the span would be much longer; recorded as a boundary judgement.

signals: unclear (BMS diagnostic fault states)
note: BMS monitoring/diagnostic function may be impaired over time; FMVSS 305 warning might not activate. Description of cause NR; only a BMS software fault affecting diagnostics is stated, too thin to map a window.

signals: motor torque request and actual; wheel speeds (slip); vehicle speed; accel/decel sequence; drive-unit fault-monitor states; supply voltage
note: MCU/VCU torque-safety-monitor thresholds trigger a safe state (loss of motive power) in specific scenarios: low-speed wheel slip on ice, decel-to-accel at low speed, repeated back-to-back max accel/decel, false drive-unit fault monitors. Found in winter road testing. Sequences of seconds. MCU is in scope.

signals: none (locates only: seat non-latch warning)
note: Defective weld on second-row seat-frame latch; found in production-verification durability testing. Cause field NR; defect text states the weld defect.

signals: none (no in-vehicle signal: label content)
note: Sun visors carry non-US or no airbag warning labels (FMVSS 208 labelling); found in plant audit.

signals: none (locates only: cabinet detachment in a crash)
note: Cabinet bolts installed without required washers after a parts deviation; assembly human error.

signals: none (locates only: leveller alarm / fluid loss)
note: Leveling-jack hydraulic hoses not routed, secured or protected; chafing and heat blistering. Heat and chafe testing by engineering and an independent lab.

signals: none (locates only: tailgate-ajar state while moving)
note: Tailgate latch pawl perpendicular to catch; pawl walkout under dynamic loading (design weakness); analysis and testing.

signals: none (no in-vehicle signal: anchorage strength)
note: Second-row seat pedestal anchor brackets too weak for FMVSS 207/210; compliance test failure.

signals: cell-module voltage and self-discharge trend across charge cycles and parked periods; module temperature during and after charging
note: HV cell modules: two possible supplier causes (particle contamination, separator damage) leading to an internal short and overheating during or after charging. The remedy is self-discharge-detection software, so the internal-short mechanism is observable as a self-discharge trend; which of the two physical causes is not. Rated as PE070. Defective part is the cell module (out of scope).

signals: none (no in-vehicle signal: seat geometry)
note: Third-row bench seating width requires three designated seating positions but has two belts; regulatory interpretation error, confirmed by external testing institute.

signals: none (locates only: CAN loss / bus-off at the event)
note: Improperly retained DCFC loopback harness connector; CAN wire chafes on frame rail and shorts, temporary CAN loss, loss of propulsion. Defective part is wiring/harness retention.

signals: battery SOC and cell-voltage fluctuation across a full discharge cycle (drive to 20 % SOC); cell/pack temperature during quick charge
note: Excessive lithium deposits in battery cells raise resistance and cause SOC fluctuation; rapid heating in Level 3 quick charging. Remedy LBC/VCM software detects SOC fluctuation over a full monitoring cycle (documents state the cycle), hence >700 s. Description-of-cause field empty; mechanism stated in defect text. Defective part is the cells (out of scope).

signals: none (locates only: gate swinging open)
note: Trailer inside gate has no secondary latch (design).

signals: none (no in-vehicle signal: guard strength)
note: Aluminium rear impact guard may not meet FMVSS 223 performance and labelling; cause stated as TBD (flagged), but any cause of guard strength is a structural property, so state 0 is mappable.

signals: none (locates only: string-open / fuse-blown warning, abnormal module voltage and temperature)
note: Same defect text as PE063 (Freudenberg module J-bar weld penetration; BMS software does not lock out the pack). Rated identically: stated cause is the weld, not signal-observable; out of scope (module internal busbar).

signals: SOC dwell at high state of charge across sessions; charging-current ripple from the charging infrastructure; cell voltages and temperatures
note: EQB HV battery cells (Farasis) may be insufficiently robust at high SOC: supplier early-production variation combined with external factors (charging-current ripple, mechanical damage); no specific root cause found. This campaign covers vehicles whose 25V-050 BMS update was not applied. The observable factors (high-SOC dwell, charging ripple) accumulate over sessions. Defective part is the cells (out of scope).

signals: none (locates only: inflator rupture at deployment)
note: Curtain-airbag inflator lots with moisture introduced at supplier; internal corrosion and stress-corrosion cracking; field parts analysed.

signals: none (no in-vehicle signal: part variant)
note: Wrong-market steering wheel and driver airbag installed from an incorrect factory parts list (FMVSS 208).

signals: none (no in-vehicle signal: headrest design)
note: Third-row headrests not to specification (padding, catch groove); vehicle not reworked after validation tests; found in plant audit.

signals: none (locates only: fairing detachment)
note: Roof fairing adhesive bond: surfaces not properly prepped. Original report said cause under investigation; amended report states it.

signals: none (no in-vehicle signal: exit location)
note: Roof emergency exit in the wrong location for FMVSS 217 (regulation misread); design noncompliance.

signals: isolation-fault DTC and fault-severity class at the trip; HV shutdown state; gear state
note: Same defect as PE043 (non-school-bus population): vehicle control software misclassifies loss of isolation as a severe fault and shuts the HV system in motion. Rated as PE043.

signals: isolation-monitor DTC (single vs double isolation) and isolation-resistance values at the warning; HV shutdown state
note: Electric-drive-motor software cannot tell a single-isolation condition from a double-isolation condition in some production configurations and shuts the HV system 15-20 s after the warning. The fault classification and isolation readings at the warning identify it. Debris in the motor from supplier production is mentioned as a contributing possibility. A real isolation condition is involved, so not software-only.

signals: none (locates only: loose belt cable fastener)
note: Front seat-belt steel cable fatigues from repeated bending over the seat structure on entry (design weakness); returned-part analysis.

signals: ICCU / LDC voltage peaks and over-current transients; power-stage temperature history across charge and drive cycles; 12 V battery voltage
note: ICCU (24V-200; ODI PE23012 open and close resumes) damaged over time by transient high voltage and thermal cycling; returned ICCUs show damage after thermal cycling and voltage peaks. Rated as PE049.

signals: BECM SOH value versus pack age/odometer; displayed SOC versus cell voltages at the power limitation
note: Service-replacement BECM initialises SOH at 100 % instead of inheriting the pack SOH; SOC over-estimated, unexpected power limitation; lithium plating over many DC fast-charge cycles (second leg, which alone would need >700 s). For the power-loss event a snapshot (SOH 100 % on an aged pack, cell voltages at the limit) identifies it. Found from connected-vehicle data.

signals: none (locates only: belt slack in a crash)
note: End-fitting pretensioner locking impaired by gas blow-by at sealing piston (supplier manufacturing variation); found in conformity-of-production and sled tests.

signals: none (locates only: inflator rupture)
note: Roof-rail airbag inflator lot may have a manufacturing defect (end-cap separation / sidewall split); root cause still under investigation (flagged). Any inflator manufacturing cause is structural, so state 0 is mappable.

signals: none (locates only: arcing / loss of HV at the junction box)
note: Missing or loose bus-bar retention nuts in the HV battery junction box after a plant rework without torque re-verification (24V-144 scope amendment). Assembly error; in scope (junction box).

signals: none (locates only: retractor lock-up on incline)
note: Seat-belt retractor assembled to the wrong seating position on a double seat (supplier assembly error).

signals: none (no in-vehicle signal: seat-back engagement)
note: Fold-away seat back frame weldment too narrow deforms the dump mechanism; back may not engage (FMVSS 207/210). Supplier recall pass-through.

signals: gate-driver signal interruptions / switching-module fault events; neighbouring-signal temperature deviation trend over the last ~100 miles; motor vibration
note: Gen 4 inverter: motor vibration causes fretting between pads and contacts on the gate-driver PCBA over time; signal interruptions then switching-module failure. A wear-out trend; the documents state a temperature-deviation proxy flags failures at least ~100 miles ahead and that a higher sampling rate improves detection. Rated as cumulative degradation (state 5).

signals: OBC fault / shutdown-request code and OBC state at the shutdown
note: An error in OBC software initiates a powertrain shutdown without warning. Mechanism stated only as a software routine; the OBC shutdown request and state at the trip would identify it. Returned parts tested.

signals: none (locates only: LIN6 communication loss and BMS limp mode)
note: Cabin electric water pump PCBA lacks conformal coating over a resistor; pump fails, LIN6 communication lost, BMS limp mode (8.5 kW). Supplier root cause; defective part is the water pump.

signals: none (locates only: buckle-switch state disagreeing with occupant)
note: Chassis pass-through (FCA 24V-129): driver seat-belt buckle sensor may not detect buckling; warning light and chime may not work. Cause NR (flagged); remedy is buckle replacement, so a part defect, mapped to state 0.

signals: none (locates only: EPCU fault / stall; coolant level drop)
note: EPCU improperly sealed by supplier; coolant leaks internally onto the circuit board; stall. Assembly/process defect; in scope (EPCU).

signals: unknown (inverter / BMS fault state at the loss of propulsion)
note: Loss of propulsion with a warning light; involved components inverter (IPU) and BMS ECU; description of cause NR; no mechanism in any of the five reports; remedy is repurchase. Too thin to map.

signals: none (no in-vehicle signal: webbing-lock function)
note: Retractor pawl spring inserted at the wrong angle by supplier; over use it can block the flywheel and disable webbing locking. Supplier testing and analysis.

signals: none (locates only: CAN loss / bus-off at the event)
note: Same defect as PE044 (non-school-bus population): improperly retained DCFC loopback harness connector chafes and shorts a CAN wire. Rated as PE044.

signals: none (locates only: door latch failure)
note: Entry-door latch handle redesign by supplier created a weak attachment point; latch may break (supplier pass-through).

signals: none (locates only: arc detection / HV shutdown at the junction box)
note: Under-torqued fasteners on the inverter-cable joint in the HV junction box (production); arcing, HV shutdown. Assembly error; in scope (junction box).

signals: none (locates only: airbag warning lamp / connector fault)
note: AC housing condensation drips onto the airbag control unit; connector corrosion over time (design did not anticipate the volume). Corrosion found on returned parts; condensation scenario reproduced.

signals: none (locates only: loose walk-board rack)
note: Walk-board rack fasteners (non-locking nuts) loosen under vibration; field inspections. Cause field NR; defect text states the mechanism.

signals: none (locates only: trim separation)
note: Quarter-window trim not properly secured at supplier (missing clear primer per population text). Cause field empty; mechanism stated in defect and population text.

signals: none (no in-vehicle signal measures propellant state; cabin humidity/temperature history would show exposure only)
note: Takata driver inflator: ammonium-nitrate propellant degrades after years of high absolute humidity and temperature cycling; rupture on deployment (coordinated remedy order filing).

signals: none (locates only: wheel-nut torque loss / wheel-end looseness)
note: Paint masking left between wheel and hub; compresses and loosens lug nuts. Found by inspection of warranty vehicles.

signals: none (locates only: DC-DC output drop under high 12 V load)
note: Mislabelled revision-B DC-DC converter with insufficient power-output margin installed; may shut off when 12 V demand exceeds capacity. Stated cause is the wrong part (supplier labelling), found by plant quality; in scope (DC-DC).

signals: none (locates only: control-arm fracture)
note: Rear lower control-arm design with insufficient water management corrodes and fractures; field survey of parts.

signals: battery charge current versus BMS current-charge-limit (CCL) during regen; inverter regen torque; BMS over-current fault; contactor state
note: Inverter firmware does not respect BMS current charge limits during regen; repeated and/or sustained excursions make the BMS open the main contactor. BMS logs showed over-current faults; testing reproduced it. The repeated excursions span seconds. Over-current is an electrical event, so not software-only.

signals: none (locates only: window detachment)
note: Sleeper bunk window interim hinge and mounting hardware insufficient to hold the window when driven open (design); warranty trend.

signals: none (no in-vehicle signal: joint strength)
note: Adhesive not properly applied between lower interior side panel and seat rail; FMVSS 221 joint strength; found in internal audit.

signals: pack / contactor current during DC fast charge and wide-open-pedal events; contactor temperature and resistance
note: Main-contactor design and part variation not robust to heat from DC fast charging and multiple wide-open-pedal events; arcing, open or welded contactor (original 22V-412; remedy software monitors contactor temperature and resistance). No accumulation over sessions stated here (unlike PE027), so the lower state for heat built within a charge or drive (minutes) is taken by the tie rule.

signals: none (locates only: isolation / over-temperature DTC at the sub-junction box)
note: Design drawing error leaves a 1.5 mm gap between bus bar and connector in the motor sub-junction box; bolt loosens, resistance and heat rise, DTC cuts motor current. Found in durability testing and teardown; in scope (junction box).

signals: end-to-end communication-monitor error-memory entry and the safety-ECU message counters/CRC status at the trip
note: Pulse-controlled inverter software monitoring end-to-end communication sporadically flags a faulty communication that is not there and shuts the powertrain down (21V-486; ODI PE21-013 open and close resumes). The error-memory entry and message status at the trip identify it; found from vehicle data.

signals: none (no in-vehicle signal: joint strength)
note: School-bus body joints fail FMVSS 221: protective film left under adhesive, missing and misplaced fasteners by an untrained employee; compliance tests.

signals: none (no in-vehicle signal: weld seams)
note: Seat-frame-base weld seams out of specification after a supplier welding machine was mis-mounted after maintenance. Cause field NR; chronology states it.

signals: none (locates only: hub heat / wheel wobble)
note: Axle hubs built without inner bearing cup/race by supplier (pass-through).

signals: regen current and pack/cell voltage at high SOC; SOC; regen torque; BMS overcharge fault and contactor state
note: BMS software does not manage regeneration at high SOC; a perceived overcharge (downhill regen) triggers shutdown. Seeing the regen current and voltage rise into the overcharge trip needs the seconds before. A charge-current/overvoltage protection trip is treated as an electrical event (as PE001, PE009), so not software-only.

signals: accelerator-pedal torque request versus inverter applied torque on CAN; operator input sequence; brake state
note: Inverter torque logic may retain a prior torque request after a particular sequence of operator inputs, giving torque above the request (up to 20 %) or a STOP SYSTEM shutdown. Confirmed from vehicle CAN data logs and replicated intermittently. A sequence of seconds.

signals: regen current and cell voltage versus the safety limit at high SOC; SOC; BMS shutdown command
note: Vehicle/BMS software commands more regen at high SOC than the battery can sustain; cell voltage exceeds the safety limit and the BMS shuts down (pass-through from 24V-399 single-purchaser request). Seconds of regen before the trip. Rated as PE036; over-voltage protection trip treated as an electrical event.

signals: none (locates only: axle shift on spring)
note: Substitute axle spring U-bolts not torqued; supplier cycle testing and returned-part inspection.

signals: none (locates only: control-arm fracture)
note: Control-arm pivot bolt not fully hardened in supplier production (process issue reported by supplier).

signals: none (locates only: pretensioner non-function in a crash)
note: Pretensioner micro gas generator incorrectly friction-welded after faulty welder maintenance at supplier. Cause field NR; chronology states it.

signals: none (locates only: inverter fault / torque loss at the event)
note: Cybertruck drive inverter stops producing torque; cause field NR, but the population and remedy single out inverters with a specific MOSFET part number (increased failure rate in field data); remedy replaces the inverter with a properly functioning MOSFET. A defective component, mapped to state 0; mechanism not given.

signals: none (locates only: clunk / control-arm separation)
note: Upper control-arm ball-joint nut under-torqued: tool-to-fastener misalignment at assembly.

signals: none (no in-vehicle signal: belt retraction geometry)
note: Driver seat / belt configurations: belt interferes between seat back and rear partition, poor retraction (FMVSS 209); integration interference analysis missed it (design).

signals: diagnostic-request traffic to the BMS on the vehicle bus; BMS reset / memory-overflow event; contactor state
note: BMS software (development-process deviation): continuous diagnostic requests from other control units overload BMS memory; the BMS resets and contactors open. Identifying it needs the request traffic leading up to the reset; no time scale stated, so the lowest sequence state is taken (tie rule). Testing reproduced reduced power / loss of propulsion.

signals: none (no in-vehicle signal: weld quality)
note: Captain-chair pedestal improperly welded to base plate at supplier (FMVSS 207/210); returned part inspected.

signals: none (locates only: arcing DTC / loss of HV at the junction box)
note: Missing or loose bus-bar retention nuts in the HV battery junction box after a plant rework (original 24V-144; PE058 is its scope amendment). Returned parts confirmed arcing at the joint. Rated as PE058.

signals: none (no in-vehicle signal: belt variant)
note: Middle-East-specification seat belts (no automatic locking retractor) installed in US vehicles; found by plant inspection.

signals: AC input voltage and current at the on-board charger across charge sessions (resistance-induced voltage drop); plug/cable temperature if sensed
note: NEMA charging cable: low-quality or outdated household receptacles raise resistance and heat the plug; repeated use eventually damages crimps permanently, raising resistance further (documents state accumulation). Remedy adds a temperature sensor in the plug. Defective part is the charging cord (out of scope).

signals: none (locates only: wheel-end looseness / wheel-off)
note: Axle spindle-nut locking tab not installed or not engaged at axle supplier (pass-through). Cause field NR; defect text states the assembly error.

signals: none (no in-vehicle signal: emblem post cracks)
note: Driver-airbag cover resin emblem posts may crack over time (Tier-2 production variation) and detach on deployment.

signals: TBM-to-HCP message exchange on the vehicle bus before the HCP reset; HCP reset event; software version
note: FOTA-updated telematics box (TBM) software causes incomplete communication with the hybrid control processor (HCP), which resets and drops motive power. A reset leaves little state, so identifying it needs the message exchange in the seconds before. Cause field empty; mechanism in defect text. Defective modules are the telematics box and vehicle-level hybrid controller: out-of-scope flag (judgement).

signals: inverter "Trap10" error code and state at the shutdown
note: Siemens ELFA2 inverter firmware: microcontroller-to-SRAM timing delivers invalid data, a "Trap10" nuisance error shuts the electric drive down. The specific error code at the trip identifies it. Supplier-notified.

signals: none (no in-vehicle signal: belt length; buckle cannot be latched)
note: Supplier shipped wrong-length rear seat-belt buckle; found by measurement.

signals: none (no in-vehicle signal: headliner energy absorption)
note: Headliner impact-absorbing plates give insufficient absorption (FMVSS 201); compliance testing.

signals: none (no in-vehicle signal: seat and anchorage strength)
note: Campervan bench seating: incorrect reinforcement, mounting hardware and belt anchor bolts (FMVSS 207/209/210); pull test.

signals: pack / contactor current during wide-open-pedal and DC fast-charge events; contactor temperature and resistance history across sessions
note: Scope amendment of 23V-687 (PE027): BEC main contactor not robust to heat from multiple wide-open-pedal and DC fast-charge events; accumulated heat damage and wear. Rated as PE027.

signals: none (locates only: overvoltage event and MPPU open at the trip)
note: Motor controller: supplier substituted non-phosphate-coated fasteners at internal bus-bar joints (material-shortage deviation); lower preload, higher joint resistance, overvoltage event, protection unit fails open. Stated cause is the fastener substitution; in scope (motor controller).

signals: BECM micro-processor reset event / reset cause and contactor-open state at the trip
note: BECM micro-processor operating-system fault resets the BECM and opens the HV contactors while driving (supplier software). The reset record at the trip identifies it. Found from five market vehicle reports.

signals: software part number (snapshot); pack / contactor current during DC fast charge and wide-open-pedal events; contactor temperature and resistance
note: Vehicles recorded as remedied under 22S41/23S56 but the service tool did not install the remedy software (and an audit-dashboard bug); the underlying contactor-overheating condition (PE015/PE027) persists. Rated on the underlying failure mechanism as PE015; the missing software itself is visible in a snapshot of the software version. Boundary judgement.

signals: battery temperature crossing 0 C; charge-enable-relay (CER) disable/enable events; VCU charge-inhibit latch state
note: VCU firmware latches the charge-enable relay off when battery temperature crosses 0 C twice within one minute; charging and regen disabled until hard reset; vehicle may run flat. The documents state the one-minute time scale, hence (40,80] s. Defect in the VCU firmware (vehicle-level controller), out-of-scope flag per my applied convention.

signals: none (no in-vehicle signal: door opening geometry)
note: Rear emergency door opening obstructed by certain seats installed near the back wall (design; FMVSS 217); found with production fixture check.

signals: occupant-detection classification and seat-sensor reading at the event; airbag-suppression state
note: Occupant detection system calibrated for leather seats installed on suede seats; may suppress the passenger airbag. The ODS classification at the moment (with the seat variant) identifies it.

signals: none (no in-vehicle signal: webbing-sensor lock)
note: Rear seat-belt webbing-sensor spring installed in the wrong position (supplier); supplier equipment recall pass-through.

signals: none (no in-vehicle signal: placard data)
note: Certification placard lists wrong front GAWR (data-entry error).

signals: none (locates only: steering drift / loose U-bolts)
note: Front-axle U-bolt axial force decays from part misalignment (centre-bolt interference with spacer) and torque variation; bench testing duplicated it.

signals: none (locates only: OCDC fault / 12 V not charging)
note: Onboard charger with integrated DC/DC (OCDC): insufficient protective PCB coating lets humidity cause electromigration; OCDC stops charging the 12 V battery. Stated cause is the coating coverage (supplier); in scope.

signals: none (no in-vehicle signal: seat-back engagement)
note: Same Freedman fold-away seat defect as BR010 (narrow back-frame weldment deforms the dump mechanism); pass-through.

signals: none (locates only: EPCU fault / fail-safe mode; coolant loss)
note: EPCU DC-DC converter housing insufficiently sealed (inadequate steam cleaning at supplier); internal coolant leak contaminates the main controller. Process defect; in scope (EPCU).

signals: MCPA (motor control processor) software version and fault state at the loss of propulsion
note: Incorrect software released into the inverter motor-control processor (MCPA) may allow loss of propulsion in certain circumstances; cause field NR, the mechanism is not described further. The stated cause (wrong software installed) is visible in a snapshot of the software version. Found by engineering analysis with no field reports.

signals: none (no in-vehicle signal: valve part number / relief setting)
note: Wrong counterbalance valve (lower relief setting) supplied as production and service part due to an incorrect supplier part number in the system; found at incoming inspection.

signals: none (locates only: contactor open under load at -40 C)
note: HV battery-pack contactors from one sub-supplier lot have a manufacturing defect in the coil terminal; at -40 C they may open under load (battery supplier recall pass-through). In scope (contactor).

signals: none (locates only: pretensioner non-function in a crash)
note: Front seat-belt pretensioner tubes damaged on one supplier production line. Cause field NR; chronology states the supplier process defect.

signals: key-cycle (ignition on/off) events across the day; control-unit sequential counter value; shutdown state
note: A sequential counter for the direct charging box in the control unit trips after excessive key cycles (customer driving ~1 km and switching off repeatedly through the day) and shuts the vehicle down. Original report: cause under investigation; amendment names the counter error. The documents state a day-long time scale of key cycles, hence >700 s (a recorded counter value at the trip could shorten this). Remedy reprograms the VCU and instrument cluster: out-of-scope flag (vehicle-level controller, judgement).

signals: contactor coil/closing current signature (single vs double dip) at each closing; rolling 100-closing window; ambient temperature
note: Contactors in which the spring force can overcome the magnetic holding force open unexpectedly; defective units show a double-dip closing-current signature. Lucid screened the fleet by OTA on a rolling 100-closing window with a 5 % threshold, so the identifying signature is high-rate current at closing, accumulated over many key cycles. In scope (contactor).

signals: none (no in-vehicle signal measures propellant state; climate history would show exposure only)
note: Takata non-desiccated PSAN passenger inflators: propellant degradation after years of high absolute humidity, temperature and temperature cycling; rupture on deployment. Returned-inflator testing (ODI EA15-001 open resume; consent-order findings in chronology).

signals: CAN traffic at ECU initialization: DC-box ECU error frames, BMS message ID and timing; VCU SoC signal
note: DC-box ECU transmits error frames to the VCU after initialization (BMS CAN ID conflict / timing); VCU shows SoC 0 % at standstill and the truck cannot be driven. Remedy changes BMS CAN timing and ID sending and relaxes the VCU error trigger. A bus sequence of seconds after key-on. BMS software is in scope, so no out-of-scope flag.

signals: none (locates only: DC-DC internal-short DTC and heat)
note: DC-DC converter rectifying module damaged in supplier production (static charge suspected) fails short; 12 V current keeps heating it; while charging with battery heater on and a clogged breather plug the case melts and the duct ignites. Supplier duplication testing; in scope (DC-DC).

signals: none (locates only: wind noise / panel detachment)
note: Front stationary roof panel re-bonded in service with wrong pretreatment, primer or adhesive; bond degrades over time (ODI PE21-001 resumes). Repair scenarios recreated in tests; returned panels analysed.

signals: none (locates only: spoiler noise / detachment)
note: Rear spoiler upper shell not welded or poorly welded to base at supplier; returned part inspected.

signals: none (locates only: seat movement / bracket dislodged)
note: Seat-belt/seat-back anchoring bracket improperly welded; seat-slider components out of tolerance from tool wear (supplier).

signals: none (no in-vehicle signal on the trailer frame; crack found by inspection)
note: Vacuum-excavator trailer frame fatigue cracks when loaded above GVWR (marginal design); strain test and FEA. Cause field NR; chronology states the analysis.

signals: none (locates only: liftgate seizure)
note: Liftgate cylinder pivot pin lacked lubricant penetration at supplier; pin may seize (supplier equipment recall pass-through).

signals: contactor economizer-coil current PWM waveform; pack current; battery thermistor nearest the contactor (repeated thermal throttling); fuse state
note: Economizer-coil electronic drivers in some HV contactors malfunction (misformed coil PWM, ringing), giving excessive contact resistance and overheating; blown fuse or BMS opens contactors. The documents describe a thermistor near the contactor repeatedly thermal-throttling before failure, i.e. heat built over a drive (minutes); the coil PWM anomaly needs a high-rate capture. Electronic contactor testing established the root cause. In scope (contactor).

signals: none (locates only: HV shutdown / short at disconnect-switch terminals)
note: Same defect as PE056 (school-bus population): fuse-box / disconnect-switch bracket fatigue; terminals short. Rated as PE056.

signals: SOC dwell at high state of charge across sessions; charging-current ripple from the charging infrastructure; cell voltages and temperatures
note: Original EQB campaign (25V-050; PE069 is its follow-on): Farasis cells may be insufficiently robust at high SOC from supplier production variation combined with external factors (charging-current ripple, mechanical damage); no specific root cause found; interim 80 % SOC limit, BMS software remedy. Rated as PE069.

signals: airbag-control-unit stored DTC versus warning-lamp / cluster message state
note: Airbag control unit software mis-programmed by supplier: a self-diagnosed restraint or pedestrian-protection fault does not light the warning lamp. A diagnostic readout showing a stored DTC with no lamp identified it.

signals: battery SOC and cell-voltage fluctuation across a full discharge cycle; cell/pack temperature during quick charge
note: Original LEAF campaign (24V-700; PE064 is its MY2021-22 follow-on): excessive lithium deposits in cells raise resistance and cause SOC fluctuation; rapid heating in Level 3 quick charging. The amended chronology records SOC fluctuations in vehicle data before some thermal events, and the remedy software needs a full monitoring cycle. Rated as PE064; cells out of scope.

signals: none (no in-vehicle signal: anchor crimp strength)
note: Pretensioner anchor cables improperly crimped by supplier; failed lot-acceptance tensile test.

signals: none (locates only: momentary over-current trip in the inverter)
note: Conductive fibrous shavings from the drive-motor slip-ring assembly momentarily short the slip rings; the inverter sees an over-current and cuts torque (fail-safe). Remedy is inverter fail-safe software. The stated cause (shavings) is debris from a motor part: a current record would show a momentary short, not its origin, so state 0. Defective part is the motor slip ring: out-of-scope flag (judgement). RMISC attachment image-only.

signals: none (locates only: seat back not latching)
note: Left-rear seat-back striker misaligned during vehicle assembly (FMVSS 207).

signals: ground-offset / electrical noise on the CAN bus and CAN error events at fail-safe entry; accelerator-pedal sequence (rapid cycling, sustained 100 %, abrupt release); motor torque
note: A deteriorating electrical ground on the power-electronics module generates electrical noise that causes CAN communication errors and fail-safe mode; in a specific pedal sequence a slow unintended acceleration can follow pedal release. Vehicle data from the incident vehicle pointed to the unstable ground; remedy adds a ground wire and EPCU software. Identifying it needs the noise/CAN errors and the pedal sequence over seconds. In scope (PE module with OBC/EPCU).

signals: BMS reset / self-diagnosis fault entry and pulse-inverter deactivation fault entry at the event
note: Two software causes: HV battery-management self-diagnosis too sensitive, causing unnecessary resets; pulse-inverter software mis-evaluates internal measurements and deactivates the inverter. Field fault entries indicated the condition; the fault entry at the event identifies it.

signals: inter-inverter CAN messages (missing frames, time-out); inverter fault state; traction contactor state
note: Inverter firmware: cumulative CAN traffic from inverter 2 overflows short-term buffer, frames are lost, firmware intolerant of missing frames, message times out and the traction contactor opens. Reproduced as a function of message time-outs. Identifying it needs the message stream over seconds before the time-out.

signals: none (locates only: HEV warning / relay heat)
note: Re-recall of vehicles that did not actually receive the Recall 178 remedy: main relays in the power relay assembly from a previous supplier have loose terminal fit (lower torque and contact-pressure specs), raising resistance and heat. Stated physical cause; in scope (relay assembly).

signals: HV pack current during repeated rapid-acceleration events across rides (fuse I2t history)
note: HV fuse rating too low: repeated rapid-acceleration events degrade the fuse until it opens (documents state cumulative degradation over repeated events, hence >700 s). Remedy is a higher-rated fuse. In scope (HV fuse).

signals: none (no in-vehicle signal: pawl material)
note: Trunk-latch pawl material contracts thermally at high ambient temperature and can be damaged (FMVSS 401); material durability tests of recovered latches.

signals: none (locates only: flattened springs / handling)
note: Trailer axles fitted with under-rated (4400 lb) springs instead of 5100 lb; wrong part.

signals: inter-inverter CAN messages (missing frames, time-out); inverter fault state; traction contactor state
note: Phase two of the PE002 defect (19V-834): inverter firmware intolerant of missing CAN frames from cumulative traffic overflowing the buffer; message time-out opens the traction contactor. Rated as PE002.

signals: none (locates only: connection heating / stall)
note: Battery cable connections at traction motors and power inverter not properly secured (manufacturing error); high resistance, heat, stall. Assembly error.

signals: none (locates only: connector C6 damage / VCU malfunction)
note: Incorrect circuit design lets continuous over-current flow through cab-harness connector C6; after about 20,000 km the pin discolours and the vehicle control unit may malfunction. Found in durability testing; design error identified by analysis. Defective part is a cab wiring harness (out of scope).

signals: none (locates only: contactor open / cannot enter drive)
note: Pack contactors with one sub-supplier solenoid have poor coil termination connections and may open suddenly; high coil resistance found at service and by failure analysis of returned contactors. Stated cause is the termination quality (state 0); a coil-current record might flag a high-resistance coil, but the documents do not use one. In scope (contactor).

signals: none (locates only: arc detection / HV shutdown at the junction box)
note: Non-school-bus population of the PE029 defect: under-torqued inverter-cable fasteners in the HV junction box after a design change without a torque update. Rated as PE029.

signals: none (locates only: roof-hatch glass breakage)
note: Roof-hatch tempered glass may have an edge defect (supplier date range); cause field NR, defect text names the edge defect.

signals: cell voltages and self-discharge / internal-short indicators while parked at high SOC, across days
note: Kona Electric HV battery: cells may have internal damage from production, raising the risk of internal short (earlier report also names BMS software); specific root cause still under investigation. The BMS update detects the early onset of an internal short while parked, so the stated mechanism is observable as a slow trend while parked at full charge. Rated as PE070/PE076. Defective part is the cells (out of scope).
